co_wonderland_roped.blurb: Wonderland (Roped) covers the roped climbing at Wonderland, in Colorado's South Platte country near Pine. The area is known largely as a slab climber's paradise, though cracks and face climbs turn up as well. Sport leads, with a solid share of trad, and grades run from 5.4 up to 5.13, with the thickest concentration between 5.9 and 5.12. Wonderland South holds the most climbs, followed by Castle View Crags and The Lucy's, while Mount Jerome Crags and Wonderland North are smaller. The wider Wonderland area spreads across roughly five square miles, so the crags are scattered rather than gathered in one place.

mo_em_st_francois_state_park.blurb: St. Francois State Park sits near Bonne Terre, Missouri, with the Big River alongside it. Bouldering leads, with a smaller set of sport routes and a few trad and top-rope lines, and plenty of beginner-friendly options. Park Boulders holds the most climbs, followed by Main Bluff, where the cliff line and a scatter of boulders share the same area; Sunset Boulder and East Bluff Bouldering are smaller. Boulder grades are mostly V1 to V4, with a few harder problems, and roped climbs run from 5.7 to 5.13, mostly 5.8 to 5.12. The park is described as shady in summer, and its southwest-facing walls as a good winter choice on sunny days.

ut_white_pine_south.blurb: White Pine South is a bouldering area high in Little Cottonwood Canyon, in Utah's Central Wasatch. The boulders are granite, set in a sub-alpine, riparian landscape with a creek and riverbank nearby. Almost all of it is boulder problems across a wide spread, from V0 up to V13, with plenty of V0 to V3, a good number around V5 to V7, and a fair handful of V8 and harder. Party Pit Area holds the most climbs, followed by Warm-up Area, with Moose Boulders and a few small blocks making up the rest. The bouldering is described as at its best in the warmer months, and the altitude keeps it a bit cooler than lower in the canyon.

wa_deception_crags.blurb: Deception Crags is a cluster of small crags at Exit 38 off I-90 near North Bend, in Washington's Central-West Cascades, with the Iron Horse Trail linking several of them. It is nearly all sport climbing, mostly between 5.9 and 5.12 with 5.10 the busiest grade, plus some easier lines. Nevermind Wall holds the most climbs, followed by Deception Wall, Substation and We Did Rock, and individual crags range from a single climb to twenty-five or more. Sun or shade can be found at any time of day or year, though several routes seep after rain and Substation's faces stay wet longer under the trees. Spring, summer and fall are the stretch described for climbing here.
